title: Grading an open-book exam: two levels of metrics and two iterations

events.label: Build the evaluation set
events.detail: 10 questions, each carrying its standard provenance — which section and paragraph the answer comes from. Golden QA pairs without provenance cannot grade retrieval.

events.label: First batch run
events.detail: 10 questions fired at the RAG system (current version: fixed 512-token chunks). No special treatment — the evaluation set behaves like an ordinary user.

events.label: 10 questions asked
events.detail: Two things come back per question: the recalled chunks and the generated answer — one for each level of evaluation.

events.label: Retrieval results to the retrieval evaluator
events.detail: The retrieval-level criterion is one line: did the chunk holding the standard provenance appear in the recall results?

events.label: Retrieval-level evaluation
events.detail: 7 of 10 provenance chunks were recalled — hit rate 7/10 = 0.7. The advanced metric MRR also asks 'at which rank'.

events.label: Generation results forwarded
events.detail: Retrieval gets its own ledger — otherwise retrieval's failures get billed to generation.

events.label: Faithfulness sampling
events.detail: Sentence-by-sentence check against the recalled chunks: question 6's answer contains 'shipping is free' — no such sentence in any recalled chunk. In the RAG context, hallucination has a precise definition: saying more than the sources say.

events.label: Relevance evaluation
events.detail: Is the answer on-topic: 8 of 10 pass. Faithfulness asks 'did it invent', relevance asks 'is it about the right thing'.

events.label: First-round report
events.detail: Retrieval hit 0.7 / faithfulness 0.8 / relevance 0.8 — the weak leg is retrieval, not generation.

events.label: Locate and fix the cause
events.detail: Of the 3 missed questions, 2 had answer sentences cut by chunk boundaries (R03's old problem) → switch to structural chunking and touch nothing else.

events.label: Second batch run
events.detail: Only the chunking changed — a single-variable controlled experiment, so any movement can be attributed.

events.label: Second-round retrieval evaluation
events.detail: 9/10 recalled: 0.7 → 0.9. The remaining 1 miss is a 'warranty' question absent from the store — a knowledge gap, not retrieval's fault.

events.label: Two-round comparison report
events.detail: Retrieval 0.7→0.9, faithfulness 0.8→0.9. Troubleshooting mantra: when retrieval metrics rise but end-to-end doesn't, check retrieval first, then faithfulness, and only then suspect the model.
